title: Getting Things Done: Get Passive in Natural Speech

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I got caught in a meeting that lasted three hours. Three hours! For a topic that could have been handled in fifteen minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: No. The equipment got broken last week and still hasn't been fixed.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Something got decided. We're getting the timetable system replaced. Which we've been asking for since last year.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: That's actually good news. When's it getting done?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: They said it would get started next month. But these things always get delayed.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: By the way — you know Amir's been working on a timetable system? He might be interested.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I know. He got invited to present it last semester but the presentation got cancelled because of the fire alarm.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Is he going to get another chance?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: He should be. His work got noticed by one of the senior lecturers. Apparently she was impressed.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: He deserves it. He's been working on it for months and hasn't got paid a single tenge.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's the thing about student projects. The work gets done, the credit gets given to someone else. Usually.

dialogue.speaker: Rustam
dialogue.text: Not this time. His name is getting put on the documentation.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Good. He worked for it. He should get recognised.

questions.text: Kamila says student project work always gets proper credit.
questions.hint: "The work gets done, the credit gets given to someone else. Usually." — a critical observation. ✅

questions.text: "I got caught in a meeting." — "got caught" emphasises:
opts: Her experience — she was involuntarily stuck there
questions.correct: Her experience — she was involuntarily stuck there
questions.hint: "Get passive emphasises the subject's experience of the event." "Got caught" = she was affected, stuck. ✅

questions.text: "The timetable system is getting replaced." — "getting replaced" is:
questions.hint: "is getting replaced" = Present Continuous get passive. Happening now/in progress. ✅

questions.text: "His name is getting put on the documentation." — "getting" here:
questions.hint: "is getting put" (informal get passive) and "is being put" (formal be passive) — both correct. "Get" is more informal/conversational. ✅

questions.text: "The equipment ___ (break) last week and still ___ (not / fix)."
questions.hint: "Get passive" past: "got broken." Present Perfect passive (be): "hasn't been fixed." ✅

questions.text: "These things always get delayed." — "get delayed" vs "are delayed":
opts: "Get delayed" = subject experiences the delay (often with frustration implied); "are delayed" is more neutral
"Get delayed" only works in past tense
questions.correct: "Get delayed" = subject experiences the delay (often with frustration implied); "are delayed" is more neutral
questions.hint: "Get" passive = experiential, often with emotional overtone. "Are delayed" = neutral. ✅
